      "name": "ADMET Property Predictor",
      "description": "Predict ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) properties for one or more small molecules using RDKit descriptors and DeepChem pre-trained models. RDKit-computed properties (fast, no model): MW, LogP, TPSA, HBA, HBD, RotBonds, Lipinski Ro5 compliance, Veber compliance. DeepChem model predictions: aqueous solubility (LogS, ESOL model), Caco-2 permeability, human intestinal absorption (HIA), blood-brain barrier penetration (BBB), CYP3A4/2D6/2C9 inhibition flags, hERG cardiotoxicity flag. Molecules are scored with a composite ADMET score (0–1) and ranked. Accepts a SMILES string or a file from molecule-variant-generator output.       "id": "file-reader",
      "name": "File Reader - Read and Parse Data Files",
      "description": "Read and parse bioinformatics data files from workspace. Supports Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), CSV, PDF, FASTA (.fasta, .fa, .fna, .faa, .ffn, .frn, .fas, .fsa), and GenBank formats. Includes automatic OCR for scanned PDFs via AWS Textract. Provides multi-stage data intake: metadata only, structure preview, or full content. Use for reading experimental data, lab reports, protocols, understanding file structure, or extracting specific information.",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "file-reading",
        "data-parsing",
        "excel",
        "word",

        "file-access",
        "lab-reports",
        "protocols"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "fileKey"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "file-search",
      "name": "File Search - Discover Files in Workspace",
      "description": "Use this tool when the user asks to find, search, list, show, or discover files in their workspace (e.g., 'find files with...', 'show me files that contain...', 'what files have...'). Searches by name, content keywords, metadata, format, topics, sections, and tags. Returns file metadata without reading full content. Essential for file discovery before using file-reader.",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "file-search",
        "file-discovery",
        "metadata-search",
        "workspace-navigation",
        "data-discovery",
        "file-management"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": []
    },
    {
      "id": "file-writer",
      "name": "File Writer - Save Reports and Documents to Workspace",
      "description": "Save text content, reports, and documents as files in the user's workspace. Use after generating a report to save it as a markdown file that users can view and download. Supports plain text and markdown format.",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "file-writer",
        "save",
        "reports",
        "documents",
        "workspace",
        "markdown",
        "output"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "filename",
        "content"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "list-pipelines",
      "name": "List Pipelines - Discover Predefined Bioinformatics Pipelines",
      "description": "List all available predefined bioinformatics pipelines. Returns pipeline names, descriptions, required inputs, and estimated duration. Use this BEFORE building a pipeline from scratch to check if a predefined pipeline already covers the user's need. Can filter by category (variant-calling, transcriptomics, genomics, epigenomics, quality-control, alignment, structural-biology).",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "pipeline",
        "workflow",
        "discovery",
        "templates",
        "predefined",
        "pipeline-management"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": []
    },
    {
      "id": "pipeline-status",
      "name": "Pipeline Status - Check Multi-Step Pipeline Progress",
      "description": "Check the status and progress of a running multi-step bioinformatics pipeline. Returns overall pipeline status, individual step statuses, progress percentage, and output files when complete. Use after start-pipeline to monitor pipeline execution.",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "pipeline",
        "pipeline-status",
        "workflow-monitoring",
        "pipeline-management",
        "execution-tracking",
        "multi-step"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "executionId"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "start-pipeline",
      "name": "Start Pipeline - Launch Multi-Step Bioinformatics Pipeline",
      "description": "Start a multi-step bioinformatics pipeline. Supports two modes: (1) pipelineId mode — pass a predefined pipeline id from list-pipelines and provide only the input parameters; the steps are loaded automatically from the registry. (2) Custom steps mode — provide an explicit steps[] array for one-off pipelines. Returns an executionId to track progress with pipeline-status tool.",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "pipeline",
        "workflow",
        "multi-step",
        "orchestration",
        "pipeline-management",
        "sequential",
        "parallel",
        "automation"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": []
    },
    {
      "id": "process-results",
      "name": "Process Results - Get Process Output Files",
      "description": "Retrieve output files and results from a completed bioinformatics process. Use when a process status shows 'completed' and you need to access the generated files (e.g., PDB structures, VCF variants, analysis reports). Returns file paths, URLs, or file content for downstream analysis.",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "process-management",
        "process-results",
        "output-retrieval",
        "file-download",
        "result-analysis"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "processId"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "process-status",
      "name": "Process Status - Check Running Process Status",
      "description": "Check the status of a long-running bioinformatics process by process ID. Use when the user asks 'is my process done?', 'what's the status of process X?', or wants to check if a process has completed. Returns process status (running, completed, failed, cancelled), progress, and error messages if applicable.",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "process-management",
        "process-status",
        "workflow-monitoring",
        "execution-tracking",
        "process-check"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "processId"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "render-file-view",
      "name": "Render File as Image — View as Picture",
      "description": "Render an EXISTING workspace file as a static image (PNG/SVG) that looks exactly like the interactive viewer — a heatmap/chart from a CSV, a slice of a FASTA sequence, a PDB structure, BAM coverage, or VCF variants. Use this to SHOW the user what their data looks like inline in chat. Pass just the file NAME (e.g. 'info_test.csv') — the tool resolves it to the workspace file automatically, so NEVER ask the user for a full storage key or path. The image is saved to the workspace and returned as a URL the response embeds. This renders a file the user already has; to generate a NEW chart from raw values, use the visualization-generator instead.",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "visualization",
        "viewer",
        "image",
        "preview",
        "heatmap",
        "sequence",
        "structure",
        "render"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "fileKey"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "tavily-search",
      "name": "Tavily Web Search",
      "description": "Search the web for scientific literature and bioinformatics information using Tavily API",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "web",
        "search",
        "tavily",
        "literature",
        "utility"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "query"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "visualization-generator",
      "name": "Visualization Generator - Create Charts and Plots",
      "description": "Generate professional charts, plots, and diagrams for scientific reports. Supports standard charts (bar, line, scatter, pie), specialized bioinformatics plots (volcano, MA, Manhattan, heatmap), workflow diagrams, and 3D molecular structures. Visualizations are saved to workspace and can be included in reports.",
      "category": "utility",
      "executionMode": "instant",
      "tags": [
        "visualization",
        "charts",
        "plots",

        "diagrams",
        "bioinformatics-plots",

      ]
    }

input.content:
#  SpCas9 (NGG) sgRNA candidates targeting human CFTR exon 11 around F508del
#  Gene: CFTR  ENSG00000001626  chr7:117,287,120-117,715,971 (GRCh38, + strand)
#  Lesion: F508del = rs113993960, chr7:117,559,591 TCTT>T (NCBI dbSNP)
#  Source sequence: UCSC getSequence hg38 chr7:117,559,350-117,559,850
#  PAM enumeration + GC: manual analysis of that sequence (not a CRISPR tool)
#  Off-target column: smarts-blast vs hg38 (blastn, evalue 10) -- NOT a CFD/MIT score
#
id	protospacer_20nt	PAM	strand	protospacer_hg38	cut_site_hg38	dist_to_F508del_bp	GC_pct	ontarget_blast	fulllength_19of20_offtargets	note
G6	CAGTTTTCCTGGATTATGCC	TGG	+	chr7:117559548-117559567	117559564/565	26	45	unique 100%/100%	none	cleanest specificity + good GC; best overall
G5	CAAAGCATGCCAACTAGAAG	AGG	+	chr7:117559634-117559653	117559650/651	56	45	unique 100%/100%	chrX:15042930 (19/20)	good GC; too far for HDR, use for knockout
G3	ATATTTTCTTTAATGGTGCC	AGG	-	chr7:117559569-117559588	117559571/572	20	30	unique 100%/100%	chr6:165129030 (19/20)	acceptable compromise
G4	TCTGTATCTATATTCATCAT	AGG	-	chr7:117559606-117559625	117559608/609	14	25	unique 100%/100%	chr3:99413821 (19/20)	low GC
G1	ATTAAAGAAAATATCATCTT	TGG	+	chr7:117559575-117559594	117559591/592	0	15	unique 100%/100%	chr2:78929118, chr3:30171847 (19/20)	cuts exactly at lesion BUT 15% GC + 2 near-identical sites
G2	AAAGATGATATTTTCTTTAA	TGG	-	chr7:117559576-117559595	117559578/579	13	15	unique 100%/100%	none full-length	15% GC, likely poor activity
#
#  CAVEAT: BLAST is not a CRISPR off-target search. blastn seeding misses many
#  3-4 mismatch sites that Cas9 still cleaves, and it does not check whether an
#  off-target locus carries an NGG PAM. Before ordering, re-score these in
#  CRISPOR / Cas-OFFinder / CHOPCHOP to obtain CFD and MIT specificity scores.

## What I did

**Target selection.** CFTR is `ENSG00000001626`, chr7:117,287,120–117,715,971 (GRCh38, + strand) — from the Ensembl tool. I targeted the **F508del** locus, since that's the allele in ~85% of CF patients. The NCBI dbSNP tool places **rs113993960 at chr7:117,559,591 (TCTT>T)**. I pulled hg38 chr7:117,559,350–117,559,850 with the UCSC Genome Browser tool and confirmed the lesion in that sequence: the codons read `ATC ATC TTT GGT GTT` = I506-I507-**F508**-G509-V510, with the deletable `CTT` at 117,559,592–594.

**Guide design — this part is my own analysis, not a tool.** There is no CRISPR tool in this platform (I checked all 89 tools across algorithm/database/utility: no CRISPOR, Cas-OFFinder, CHOPCHOP, or guide scorer). So I enumerated every NGG PAM on both strands within ±60 bp of the cut target by hand from the retrieved sequence, extracted the 20-nt protospacers, and computed GC content manually.

**Validation.** All six protospacers were BLASTed against hg38 (`smarts-blast`, blastn, E-value 10). Every one returned a unique 100%-identity/100%-coverage hit at precisely the coordinate I predicted from the manual enumeration — independent confirmation that the extraction and strand assignments are correct.

| ID | Protospacer (5'→3') | PAM | Str | Protospacer (hg38) | Cut site | Δ to F508del | GC | Full-length 19/20 off-targets |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G6** | CAGTTTTCCTGGATTATGCC | TGG | + | chr7:117,559,548–567 | 117,559,564/565 | 26 bp | 45% | **none** |
| G5 | CAAAGCATGCCAACTAGAAG | AGG | + | chr7:117,559,634–653 | 117,559,650/651 | 56 bp | 45% | chrX:15,042,930 |
| G3 | ATATTTTCTTTAATGGTGCC | AGG | − | chr7:117,559,569–588 | 117,559,571/572 | 20 bp | 30% | chr6:165,129,030 |
| G4 | TCTGTATCTATATTCATCAT | AGG | − | chr7:117,559,606–625 | 117,559,608/609 | 14 bp | 25% | chr3:99,413,821 |
| G1 | ATTAAAGAAAATATCATCTT | TGG | + | chr7:117,559,575–594 | 117,559,591/592 | **0 bp** | 15% | chr2:78,929,118; chr3:30,171,847 |
| G2 | AAAGATGATATTTTCTTTAA | TGG | − | chr7:117,559,576–595 | 117,559,578/579 | 13 bp | 15% | none full-length |

**Recommendation: G6.** It is the only candidate with both no near-identical genomic competitor and workable GC (45%); its next-best BLAST hit covers only 18/20 nt. G1 is tempting because it cuts exactly on the lesion — ideal HDR geometry — but at 15% GC it will likely have poor cleavage efficiency, and it has two full-length 19/20 matches elsewhere in the genome. If you need a cut closer to the lesion than G6's 26 bp, G3 at 20 bp is the better compromise than G1.

Saved to `crispr/CFTR_F508del_sgRNA_candidates.tsv` in the **Mors Lab** workspace.

## Important limitation on the off-target scoring

**I could not compute true off-target scores.** CFD and MIT specificity scores require a mismatch-tolerant genome-wide search, which no tool here provides. BLAST is a weak proxy and understates risk in two specific ways:

- blastn's seeding **misses many 3–4 mismatch sites** that Cas9 cleaves efficiently — exactly the class that matters most.
- It does **not check whether off-target loci carry an NGG PAM**, so the hits above are neither confirmed cleavable nor an exhaustive list.

The ranking above is therefore a *genomic-uniqueness screen*, not a validated specificity score. Before ordering oligos, re-score these six in CRISPOR, Cas-OFFinder, or CHOPCHOP for real CFD/MIT values. Also note the AT-rich context here caps achievable GC at ~45% — and for F508del correction specifically, base/prime editing or HDR with ssODN is more clinically relevant than blunt Cas9 cutting, since a DSB in exon 11 risks knocking out the remaining allele.

## ANSWER

**Recommended sgRNA (SpCas9, CFTR exon 11 / F508del, hg38):**

- **G6 — `CAGTTTTCCTGGATTATGCC` + PAM `TGG`**, + strand, protospacer chr7:117,559,548–117,559,567, cut at 117,559,564/565 (26 bp from F508del), GC 45%, unique in hg38 with no full-length near-identical off-target.

Five alternates (G5, G3, G4, G1, G2) are tabled above; G3 (`ATATTTTCTTTAATGGTGCC`/AGG, 20 bp from lesion) is the best closer-cutting option. Full table: `crispr/CFTR_F508del_sgRNA_candidates.tsv` (Mors Lab workspace).

Target grounding: CFTR `ENSG00000001626` (Ensembl); F508del `rs113993960` chr7:117,559,591 (dbSNP); sequence from UCSC hg38; uniqueness from `smarts-blast` vs hg38-20211104.

**Off-target caveat: no CFD or MIT specificity score was computed — no such tool exists in this session.** PAM enumeration and GC are my manual analysis (coordinates BLAST-verified); the off-target column is a BLAST uniqueness screen only and must be re-scored in CRISPOR or Cas-OFFinder before synthesis.
